The smallest prime factor of a whole num.why: Definitional: the prime factors of a number are the primes in its factorization, so the smallest prime factor is the smallest of them. It cannot give way.

notes: Derived edit (very_likely): the smallest prime factor of 1001 is almost never stated, while its factorization 1001 = 7 × 11 × 13 is a well-known curiosity. Not from the scouting (which had no usable derived number fact); the review dropped the 'native of' history records as weak, and this replaces them with a lexical derived relation of the kind the review asked for. Mathematics leaves out worlds: a fact about a number or a class of numbers rests on definitions and proofs, so no premise can give way and the edit leaves no consistent world to split between (README, Shape per topic). Derived queries ask what the edit forces through the definitions, holding the definitions fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. So there are no worlds. The premise-route query asks whether 7 divides 1001: before the edit that is how 7 is the smallest prime factor; after it, a number has no prime factor below its smallest one. The combining premise is the definition of the smallest prime factor, which cannot give way (README Decisions 2). Plausibility: someone who skips 7 in trial division lands on 11. R1: all answers are plain arithmetic. The near query (1000) shares the relation, does not follow from the edit, and its reference (2) differs from the new answer (R6). Verifier: added a premise-route query that goes through the factorization by description (the first prime of 1001's factorization in increasing order); 'Is 1001 divisible by 7?' now asks the premise directly (derivation premise, determinate); the 1001 × 1001 query was dropped to diversify derivations (B3). R4: small models may compute rather than recall the smallest prime factor; the pre-edit audit may drop the record for them.
